Add Marginal Likelihood to brma Objects

Source: R/marglik.R
add_marglik.brma.Rd

Compute the marginal likelihood of a brma model using bridge sampling and store the result in the object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brma'
add_marglik(
  object,
  parallel = NULL,
  cores = NULL,
  repetitions = 1L,
  method = c("normal", "warp3"),
  maxiter = 10000L,
  silent = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a brma model object.

parallel

whether bridge-density evaluations run in parallel. The default, NULL, inherits the setting used to fit object.

cores

number of bridge-sampling worker processes. The default, NULL, inherits the fitted core count and is capped by RoBMA.get_option("max_cores"). It is used only when parallel = TRUE.

repetitions

number of independent bridge-sampling repetitions.

method

bridge transformation; either "normal" or "warp3".

maxiter

maximum number of bridge iterations per repetition.

silent

whether bridge-sampling progress is suppressed. The typed iteration-limit diagnostic remains visible even when silent = TRUE.

...

reserved for future use. Unused arguments produce a warning.

Value

The brma object with the marginal likelihood result stored in object[["marglik"]].

Details

The marginal likelihood is computed using the bridgesampling package via the BayesTools::JAGS_bridgesampling wrapper. The result is stored in the object and can be extracted using bridge_sampler.brma. Proposal draws use the seed stored with the fit. When that seed is non-NULL, the caller's random-number state is restored after the call; a NULL fit seed uses and advances the caller's random-number stream. A finite bridge estimate remains available when observed iteration counts exceed maxiter. The stored result's success records finite availability, not certified convergence. Its optional iteration_limit_exceeded is TRUE for observed excess, FALSE for complete counts without excess, and NA or absent when telemetry is unavailable. Counts may include upstream retries. Observed excess raises BayesTools_marglik_iteration_limit, inheriting from BayesTools_marglik_diagnostic, under either silent setting. Inspect print(object[["marglik"]]) and its repetition diagnostics. bridge_sampler(object) returns the original upstream bridge object; it does not promise the stored wrapper's optional telemetry field.

Product-space model-averaging objects (BMA.norm, BMA.glmm, BMA.mv, RoBMA, and RoBMA.mv) do not expose a bridge-sampling marginal likelihood; use predictive comparison methods such as loo.brma instead. For a single model whose bridge parameters are all fixed by point priors, the log marginal likelihood is evaluated exactly at those fixed values; no bridge-sampling repetitions are required. For brma.mv() known-V objects, bridge sampling evaluates the joint likelihood corresponding to the fitted known-V backend, not the conditional estimate-wise target used by LOO/WAIC diagnostics. Sampled Gaussian location random-effect blocks are integrated exactly during bridge evaluation as their draw-specific \(ZGZ'\) covariance. Their SD, allocation, and correlation parameters remain bridge coordinates; only the standardized latent effects are removed. This is a reparameterization of the same marginal-likelihood target, not a likelihood approximation. Fitted estimate-level marginalized blocks remain in the diagonal row variance. For Gaussian models fitted with the specialized cluster interface, the standardized cluster effects are likewise integrated exactly. The bridge retains total heterogeneity and its allocation while evaluating the implied diagonal-plus-cluster-rank-one covariance, including row-specific scale regression and likelihood weights. Selection models retain every context that the fitted model conditions on, including its normalized prior, and integrate only the Gaussian sources declared by that model. The likelihood uses the same full publication events and integration plan as fitting. A context integrated before selection normalization cannot be replaced by a retained-context parameterization. With known_sampling_variance = "condition", the bridge retains the independent Gaussian augmentation coordinates and their normalized priors. The complete sampling error and random effects are reconstructed for each proposed bridge state before evaluating its selection normalizer.

A non-finite bridge repetition raises a RoBMA_marglik_repetition_failure error, inheriting from RoBMA_marglik_error. Its parent retains the complete upstream condition, including the failed repetitions table. Increase maxiter when a failed repetition reached its iteration limit; otherwise inspect the posterior samples and priors for non-finite densities. Fitting more posterior draws (for example with a larger sample or update()) may help in either case. These actions do not guarantee that the diagnostics will pass.

A checked posterior sample that cannot form a full-rank bridge proposal raises RoBMA_marglik_rank_deficiency, inheriting from RoBMA_marglik_error. Its unchanged upstream parent and exposed reason, rank, n_coordinates, n_draws, and dependent_coordinates describe the observed sample. For reason = "insufficient_draws", fit more posterior draws with a larger sample or update(); dependence may persist. For reason = "dependent_coordinates", inspect the parameterization and sampling; more draws alone need not resolve dependence. The message names the first reported pivot coordinates; they identify one dependent set, not uniquely faulty nodes.

The stored result records an identity of the data, weights, priors, and model it was computed for. bridge_sampler(), logml(), bf(), and post_prob() refuse a stored result that no longer matches the object, or that an earlier RoBMA version stored, with an error of class RoBMA_marglik_stale (inheriting from RoBMA_marglik_error); recompute it with add_marglik(). update(slab = ) keeps it, and extending the fit with update() recomputes or drops it.

See also

bridge_sampler.brma, logml.brma, bf.brma, post_prob.brma

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(dat.lehmann2018, package = "metadat")
  fit <- brma(yi = yi, vi = vi, data = dat.lehmann2018, measure = "SMD")

  fit <- add_marglik(fit)

  bridge <- bridge_sampler(fit)
  print(bridge)

  logml(fit)
}
} # }
